name: overflow-acetate-vs-growth
title: Does v2ecoli reproduce the aerobic acetate-overflow curve (acetate-carbon yield vs growth rate) — Vemuri 2006 / Basan 2015?
question:
Across a glucose-uptake-rate titration, does v2ecoli reproduce the aerobic
acetate-overflow response — the acetate-carbon yield rising ~linearly with
growth rate above a critical threshold (Vemuri 2006 primary, Basan 2015
context) — and how do the FBA baseline, the Millard kinetic ODE, and the
v2ecoli+Millard FBA-bridge arms compare?

report.title: overflow-acetate-vs-growth — v2ecoli acetate response vs Vemuri 2006 / Basan 2015
report.caveat:
Two findings from the 2026-07-22 run limit how much this verdict carries
(recorded as findings[] `gur-knob-does-not-titrate-growth` and
`carbon-created-under-binding-uptake-cap`).

1. THE TITRATION DOES NOT TITRATE GROWTH. Across a 5.6x glucose-uptake range
   (caps 1-6; the cap binds exactly at 1-4, goes slack above ~5.6) the emergent
   growth rate moves only 0.954 -> 0.925 /h, non-monotonically. Division runs on
   the D-period replication clock (`d_period=True`, the vEcoli default), where the
   dry-mass threshold is deliberately ignored (v2ecoli/steps/division.py:181-190),
   so mean division time — and hence the mu this study reads out — is set by
   replication timing, not carbon supply. The acetate-vs-growth-rate framing
   assumes carbon uptake drives mu; in this model it does not. The graded x-range
   is therefore ~0.03 /h wide, all of it above the reference onset (mu 0.408).

2. CARBON BALANCE FAILS UNDER A BINDING CAP. At cap=1 the model takes up
   6.0 mmolC/gDCW/h as glucose and secretes 11.6 mmolC/gDCW/h as CO2 — about 2x
   the carbon in, while still growing — tripping the assumption-free
   `violation_C_created` flag. CO2 output RISES as glucose is restricted
   (11.62 / 5.00 / 1.82 at caps 1 / 2 / 6). Biomass yield tracks the same
   non-physicality: 5.30 / 2.59 / 0.92 gDW/g glucose at caps 1 / 2 / 6, against a
   measured literature band of 0.355-0.444 and a stoichiometric ceiling of 0.538.
   DIAGNOSIS IS OUT OF SCOPE HERE — it belongs to the sibling investigation
   `metabolism-biomass-yield` (v2ecoli#421), which has since resolved it to two
   distinct defects. This study records the observation and points there.

The verdict below (acetate = 0.0 at every cap, so "no overflow") is the PREDICTED
baseline-FBA outcome and is consistent with the basal card, but it is graded on a
degenerate sweep. Read it as "overflow physiology is absent", not as a quantitative
curve comparison.
report.objective:
Sweep the carbon-uptake knob (the glucose-uptake cap) and read out the
acetate-secretion response as a function of the resulting growth rate, for
three arms (baseline FBA / Millard kinetic ODE / v2ecoli+Millard FBA-bridge).
Grade each arm's response CURVE against the reference overflow curve with the
`threshold_linear` criterion (supra-threshold linearity + yield slope; the
threshold position reported but non-gating). A CHARACTERIZATION of where the
model reproduces overflow physiology — state + trend, not a pass/fail.
report.setup:
Control knob = the ExchangeData step's aerobic glucose-uptake cap, swept via a
bespoke runner (declarative sweeps were not runnable in the framework when this
ran, so a script executes the titration). Reference x-axis = growth rate (an
emergent model output at each knob setting), matching how the references report
the curve — and matching the causal direction of Basan's experiment, which
titrates transporter EXPRESSION (Pu-ptsG, inducer 3MBA) -> carbon uptake ->
emergent growth rate (a chemostat would invert this: clamp growth, let uptake
follow). Arms reuse the composites from ketchup-baseline-comparison: baseline
FBA (ecoli_baseline), the Millard kinetic ODE, and the live FBA-bridge
(millard_fba_bridge_harness). Reference = the ecoli-sources
`perturbation__overflow__acetate_vs_growth` slot: Vemuri 2006 (MG1655
glucose-limited chemostat) is the PRIMARY graded curve — it co-measures glucose
uptake, so the acetate-carbon yield Y_ac = (2*acetate)/(6*glucose) is raw per
point; Basan 2015 `ptsG_glucose` (NCM3722) rides along as context via the SI
closed form, plus an independent MG1655 13C anchor. Grading is shape-first on the
dimensionless Y_ac, which cancels per-OD vs per-gDCW on both sides — so the
OD600->gDCW factor flagged in inputs/notes/basan2015.md is NOT needed (resolved
2026-06-24; that note is superseded).
Key test: overflow is a constraint phenomenon — plain growth-max FBA respires
fully and excretes no acetate (the ketchup baseline finding), so this grades
whether v2ecoli encodes the proteome/respiration limit that makes overflow
emerge (baseline-FBA predicted no overflow; the kinetic/bridge arms may differ).

assumptions.text:
The acetate exchange flux (ACET[p], listeners.fba_results.external_exchange_fluxes)
is the model observable for overflow; growth rate is read from the mass listener.

A glucose-uptake-rate titration moves the model along a growth-rate axis
comparable to the references', on the existing glucose ParCa cache — no new data
bundle needed for this condition. (Mirrors Basan's transporter-titration causal
direction: set uptake -> growth emerges.)

The OD600->gDCW factor used to convert Basan's reported Jac (mM/OD600/h) to the
model's acetate exchange flux (mmol/gDCW/h) is an EXTERNAL assumption (not in
Basan 2015) — either import a sourced NCM3722 factor or grade in per-OD units
by converting the model side. See inputs/notes/basan2015.md.

model_settings.name: glucose-uptake-titration
model_settings.detail: The swept control knob: the ExchangeData step's `glc_uptake_cap_aerobic` config field (v2ecoli#420), titrated across the physiological range on the existing glucose ParCa cache (out/cache). Executed by sims/run_gur_titration.py, which delivers the cap per level as a native `config_overrides` variant.

model_settings.name: millard-arm
model_settings.detail: Millard 2017 central-carbon kinetic ODE arm (the flux source behind the FBA-bridge). Included to test whether the kinetic core induces overflow the baseline FBA misses. UNBUILT.

model_settings.name: overflow-reference-curves
model_settings.detail: Reference: the ecoli-sources `perturbation__overflow__acetate_vs_growth` slot (ecoli-sources#4). PRIMARY graded curve = Vemuri 2006, MG1655 glucose-limited chemostat — it co-measures glucose uptake, so the acetate-carbon yield Y_ac = (2*acetate)/(6*glucose) is raw per row, needing no model and no OD600->gDCW factor. CONTEXT = Basan 2015 `ptsG_glucose` (NCM3722), converted to Y_ac via the Supplementary-Note-1 carbon-partition closed form, plus an independent MG1655 13C anchor (Long/LaCroix/Crown). The `carbon_source` / `carbon_source_aa` Basan series are not graded here.

model_settings.name: threshold-linear-criterion
model_settings.detail: Grading: the `threshold_linear` criterion (v2ecoli#419), which fits y = max(0, slope*(x - x0)) and emits a within_tol/drift/mismatch verdict from the swept {x: growth rate, y: Y_ac} against the reference curve. Primary = worst-of(supra-threshold linearity R^2, yield-slope relative delta); threshold position reported but NON-gating. Reference-aware: absence of the rise across a sweep spanning past the reference threshold is a mismatch, not a pass. Surfaced to the framework via the `report_card_axis` workspace evaluator.

tests.name: v2ecoli-reproduces-acetate-overflow-onset
tests.question: Does v2ecoli's acetate response show the overflow rise (acetate-carbon yield rising above a critical growth rate)?

measure.detail: Overflow group graded by the threshold_linear criterion (shape-first on the dimensionless acetate-carbon yield Y_ac vs growth rate; threshold reported but non-gating) vs Vemuri 2006 primary / Basan 2015 context. Group verdict = worst axis. Baseline-FBA arm only so far; Millard / FBA-bridge arms unbuilt.

tests.name: carbon-balance-closes-under-titration
tests.question: Across the uptake titration, does the model's carbon bookkeeping close — i.e. is secreted carbon never greater than carbon taken up?

measure.detail: Assumption-free check computed per cap by the titration runner: sum of secreted C-exchange fluxes vs glucose-C uptake. Needs no biomass C-content assumption; if C_out > C_in, carbon was created.

tests.name: biomass-yield-within-stoichiometric-ceiling
tests.question: Is the emergent biomass yield Yxs at or below the stoichiometric ceiling for aerobic glucose growth?

measure.detail: Yxs = mu / (|q_glc| * M_glc). Ceiling 0.538 gDW/g_glucose = Varma 1993, the ecoli-sources basal__biomass_yield slot's single `kind: theoretical_max` row (FBA, fully aerobic, no maintenance energy). For context the four `kind: measured` rows in the same slot span 0.355-0.444 (Varma 1994, Kavvas 2022, LaCroix 2015, Long 2017).

gur-cap-binds-at-every-generation.note: cap=2 -> glucose exactly -2.0 at gen_lb=0 AND gen_lb=1 (pre-#293: -3.51 pooled, gen-1 -4.61). cap=6 slack -> -5.59 = FBA optimum.

v2ecoli-reproduces-acetate-overflow-onse.note: Card verdict mismatch — 'no overflow (yield <= 0.005 through x=0.954; ref overflows)'. Acetate 0.0 at all 6 caps. This is the PREDICTED baseline-FBA outcome, but see the caveat: graded on a ~0.03/h wide x-range.

carbon-balance-closes-under-titration.note: cap=1 trips violation_C_created: C_out 11.83 > C_in 6.0 mmolC/gDCW/h. Closure degrades monotonically as the cap tightens (1.11 / 1.26 / 1.53 / 2.31 / 3.59 / 7.93 at caps 6 -> 1).

biomass-yield-within-stoichiometric-ceil.note: Yxs = 0.92 / 1.04 / 1.29 / 1.71 / 2.59 / 5.30 gDW/g glucose at caps 6 -> 1; measured band 0.355-0.444, stoichiometric ceiling 0.538. Even the slack-cap value (0.92) is ~1.7x the ceiling.

findings.statement:
The v2ecoli baseline FBA exhibits NO aerobic acetate overflow anywhere in a
glucose-uptake titration: acetate is identically 0.0 mmol/gDCW/h at all six
caps, so the acetate-carbon yield stays flat at 0 while the Vemuri 2006
reference rises to ~0.25 above an onset of 0.408 /h. This confirms the
pre-registered prediction (and the ketchup-baseline-comparison prior that
v2ecoli secretes 0.0 acetate per 100 glucose where the KETCHUP cores secrete
~+71): overflow is a constraint phenomenon, and unconstrained growth-max FBA
respires fully rather than spilling carbon.

evidence.observed: acetate 0.0 mmol/gDCW/h at caps 1,2,3,4,5,6; card verdict mismatch — 'no overflow (yield <= 0.005 through x=0.954; ref overflows)'; reference onset mu=0.408 /h, reference yield slope 1.31

expected.summary: Y_ac rising from ~0 to ~linear above the reference onset (Vemuri 2006 MG1655 chemostat, primary graded curve)

findings.next_action: Build the Millard kinetic-ODE and FBA-bridge arms to test whether a kinetic central-carbon core induces the overflow the baseline FBA misses.

findings.statement:
THIS FINDING REFUTES THIS STUDY'S OWN SECOND DESIGN ASSUMPTION — that a
glucose-uptake titration moves the model along a growth-rate axis comparable to
the references'. It is FALSE for v2ecoli. This is a refutation of our premise,
not a disagreement with a reference.

Across a 5.6x uptake range the emergent growth rate moves only 0.954 -> 0.925 /h,
non-monotonically. The cause is by design, not a bug: division runs with
d_period=True (the vEcoli default), so it fires on the D-period replication
clock and the dry-mass threshold is deliberately ignored (the `threshold=nan fg`
in every DIVISION log line; see v2ecoli/steps/division.py:181-190). Mean division
time — and hence the mu this study reads out — is therefore set by replication
timing, not carbon supply, and cells divide on schedule at ~695 fg regardless of
how tightly glucose is capped.

Consequence for the instrument: an acetate-vs-growth-rate card cannot be driven
by a carbon knob in this model. All six sweep points land in a ~0.03 /h band,
entirely above the reference onset, so the `overflow-absent-across-titration`
verdict is graded on a degenerate x-range. Adding seeds or generations will not
help — the axis is structurally pinned, not noisy.

evidence.observed: growth rate 0.954 / 0.933 / 0.924 / 0.931 / 0.927 / 0.925 per h at caps 1-6 while glucose uptake spans -1.0 to -5.59 mmol/gDCW/h (5.6x); x-range 0.030 /h vs a reference onset at 0.408 /h
evidence.smoking_gun: division.py runs d_period=True, which sets threshold=float('nan') and gates division on the replication clock rather than dry mass

findings.next_action: Decide how mu should be made carbon-responsive for perturbation cards — mass-gated division (d_period=False, accepting the early-division regression the code comment describes, and noting `division` is absent from _CACHE_CONFIG_NAMES so this is a code change not a config flip), or re-axis the card onto the knob (Y_ac vs GUR) instead of emergent growth rate.

findings.statement:
Under a binding glucose cap the model creates carbon. At cap=1 it takes up
6.0 mmolC/gDCW/h as glucose and secretes 11.83 mmolC/gDCW/h of carbon — 11.62 of
it as CO2 — while still growing at 0.954 /h and therefore also building biomass
carbon. This trips the assumption-free `violation_C_created` flag, which compares
secreted C-exchange against C uptake and needs no biomass C-content assumption.

The effect is inverted with respect to carbon supply: CO2 output RISES as glucose
is restricted (11.62 / 5.00 / 1.82 mmol/gDCW/h at caps 1 / 2 / 6), and the carbon
closure fraction degrades monotonically as the cap tightens (1.11 -> 7.93 across
caps 6 -> 1). At the slack cap the books nearly close; the tighter the constraint,
the more carbon appears from nowhere. Undiagnosed here. Candidate mechanisms: FBA
infeasibility handling under a binding bound, non-FBA replenishment of metabolite
pools, or per-gDCW flux normalisation against a stale mass.

evidence.observed: cap=1: C_in 6.0 vs C_out 11.83 mmolC/gDCW/h (violation_C_created=true); closure fraction 7.93 / 3.59 / 2.31 / 1.53 / 1.26 / 1.11 at caps 1 -> 6; CO2 11.62 / 5.00 / 1.82 at caps 1 / 2 / 6
evidence.smoking_gun: secreted carbon exceeds carbon taken up while the cell is simultaneously accumulating biomass — a mass-balance violation independent of any biomass composition assumption

expected.summary: C_out <= C_in at every cap (no carbon creation); violation_C_created false throughout

findings.next_action: Diagnosis moved OUT of this investigation 2026-07-28 — it seeds the sibling investigation `metabolism-biomass-yield` (v2ecoli#421). A model that creates carbon cannot be meaningfully asked a carbon-partitioning question, so this gates the overflow study rather than the other way round.

findings.statement:
Emergent biomass yield exceeds the stoichiometric ceiling at every cap, and the
excess grows as carbon is restricted: Yxs = 0.92 / 1.04 / 1.29 / 1.71 / 2.59 /
5.30 gDW per g glucose at caps 6 -> 1, against a measured literature band of
0.355-0.444 (Varma 1994, Kavvas 2022, LaCroix 2015, Long 2017 — the four
`kind: measured` rows of the ecoli-sources basal__biomass_yield slot) and a
stoichiometric ceiling of 0.538 (Varma 1993, the slot's single
`kind: theoretical_max` row). Even at the slack cap, where the FBA runs at its
unconstrained optimum and the carbon books nearly close, the yield is ~1.7x the
ceiling; at cap=1 it is ~10x.

This is the same defect the basal vs_literature card already reports (biomass
yield over the limit), but the titration shows it is not a fixed offset — it is
a function of how hard the carbon constraint binds, which points at the same
bookkeeping problem as `carbon-created-under-binding-uptake-cap` rather than at
a mis-parameterised biomass composition.

expected.summary: measured aerobic glucose biomass yield, ecoli-sources basal__biomass_yield slot (4 `kind: measured` sources); stoichiometric ceiling 0.538 (Varma 1993, the slot's `kind: theoretical_max` row)

findings.next_action: SUPERSEDED 2026-07-29. The former next_action — 'check whether the basal card's yield violation moves with the same knob; the two cards are likely reporting one underlying defect' — has been PERFORMED and its premise DISCONFIRMED by v2ecoli#421's S1 diagnostic (two distinct defects, not one). The live follow-up is #421's S3, scoped to maintenance-ATP / NGAM-GAM and respiratory capacity — NOT mass accounting. Nothing further is owed by this study.
